subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond?\n[Note: source PDF omits the option letter for the fourth choice – retained as printed]
explanation: Ammoniacal copper(I) chloride is the specific confirmatory test for a terminal carbon-carbon triple bond: the acidic terminal alkyne hydrogen is displaced by copper(I), forming a distinctive reddish-brown/pink precipitate of copper acetylide, a reaction that alkenes do not give. Bromine gas and bromine water decolourize with any carbon-carbon multiple bond (both alkenes and alkynes), so they confirm unsaturation generally but cannot distinguish a triple bond from a double bond, while acidified KMnO4 also oxidizes both alkenes and alkynes non-specifically. This tests the distinction between general unsaturation tests (bromine water/KMnO4, positive for both alkenes and alkynes) and the one test unique to terminal triple bonds (ammoniacal Cu(I) or Ag(I) salts, giving a precipitate specifically with alkynes). Exam tip: whenever a question asks for a test that confirms a triple bond specifically (not just 'unsaturation'), look for ammoniacal copper(I) or silver salts as the precise answer.

question_text: What volume of 0.5mol dm-3 H2SO4 will exactly neutralize 20 cm3 of 0.1mol dm-3 NaOH solution?
explanation: Using moles of NaOH = 0.1 mol/dm3 x 0.020 dm3 = 0.002 mol, and since H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O (1:2 ratio), moles of H2SO4 needed = 0.001 mol; volume of H2SO4 = 0.001 mol / 0.5 mol/dm3 = 0.002 dm3 = 2.0 cm3. subject: Chemistry
topic: Kinetic theory of matter and gases
question_text: A given volume of methane diffuses in 20s. How long will it take the same volume of sulphur (VI) oxide to diffuse under the same conditions?\n[C=12, H=1, S=32, O=16]
explanation: By Graham's Law, time taken to diffuse is directly proportional to the square root of molar mass: t(SO2) = t(CH4) x sqrt(M(SO2)/M(CH4)) = 20s x sqrt(64/16) = 20s x 2 = 40s, since sulphur(VI) oxide (SO2, molar mass 64) is four times heavier than methane (CH4, molar mass 16). A common error is using the molar mass ratio directly without taking its square root, or inverting the rate/time relationship (heavier gases diffuse slower, meaning they take longer, not less time). This tests careful application of Graham's Law of diffusion, a frequently miscalculated topic due to the inverse square-root relationship between rate and molar mass. Exam tip: always take the square root of the molar mass ratio, and remember heavier gas = longer diffusion time.
source_label: JAMB Quest · supplied keyed answer pairs · August 2026

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Chlorine consisting of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37 in the ratio 3:1 has an atomic mass of 35.5. Calculate the relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37.
explanation: Given a 3:1 ratio of the mass-35 to mass-37 isotopes, the total is divided into 4 equal parts, of which the mass-37 isotope makes up exactly 1 part, giving a relative abundance of 1/4 x 100% = 25%, consistent with the weighted average check: (35 x 75% + 37 x 25%)/100 = 35.5, matching the given atomic mass exactly. A common error is confusing which isotope's abundance is being asked for and selecting 75% (the mass-35 abundance) instead of 25% (the mass-37 abundance actually requested). This tests both ratio-to-percentage conversion and the weighted average (relative atomic mass) formula for isotopes. Exam tip: always re-read the question to confirm which specific isotope's abundance is being asked for, since both values typically appear as tempting distractor options.

question_text: 226/88 Ra → x/86 Rn + alpha-particle\nWhat is x?

subject: Physics
question_text: Calculate the angle of minimum deviation for a ray which is refracted through an equiangular prism of refractive index 1.4
explanation: An equiangular (equilateral) prism has apex angle A = 60°. At minimum deviation, n = sin[(A+Dm)/2] / sin(A/2), so sin[(60+Dm)/2] = 1.4 × sin(30°) = 0.7. Taking the inverse sine gives (60+Dm)/2 ≈ 44.4°, so Dm ≈ 2(44.4) − 60 ≈ 28.9°, rounding to 29°. This is the same standard prism-deviation formula used throughout minimum-deviation problems, just with a different refractive index than usual.

question_text: The change in volume when 450kg of ice is completely melted is [density of ice = 900 kgm⁻³, density of water = 1000 kgm⁻³]

question_text: In a hydraulic press, a force of 40N is applied on the effort piston of area 0.4m². If the force exerted on the load piston is 400N, the area of the large piston is
explanation: By Pascal's principle, pressure is transmitted equally throughout an enclosed fluid: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, so A₂ = F₂A₁/F₁ = (400 × 0.4)/40 = 4m². subject: Physics
question_text: A ray of light makes an angle of 35° with a plane mirror. What is the angle of reflection?
explanation: The angle of incidence and reflection are always measured from the normal (perpendicular to the mirror surface), not from the mirror surface itself. If the ray makes 35° with the mirror surface, it makes 90° − 35° = 55° with the normal, so both the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection are 55°. This normal-vs-surface distinction is a classic trap — always convert an angle given relative to the surface into the equivalent angle relative to the normal before applying the law of reflection.

subject: Physics
question_text: When the human eye loses its power of accommodation, the defect is known as:
explanation:
Accommodation is the eye's ability to change the lens curvature using the ciliary muscle so that near and distant objects are brought into focus.
Presbyopia is the age‑related loss of lens elasticity and therefore of accommodation, producing difficulty in focusing on nearby objects.
Physically the crystalline lens hardens and the near point recedes, so even with active effort the eye cannot increase its optical power enough for close work.
Presbyopia is commonly corrected with convex (plus) reading glasses, bifocals or multifocal lenses which supply the extra converging power the stiff lens can no longer provide.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
explanation: the electromagnetic spectrum orders waves by frequency (and inversely by wavelength) with c = fλ linking them. X-rays are the correct choice because they lie above ultraviolet in the spectrum and therefore have higher frequencies than UV, infrared and radio. Frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength, so the much shorter wavelengths of X-rays correspond to much higher frequencies than infrared or radio waves.\n\nUltraviolet has higher frequency than visible light but remains lower than X-rays, making it the most plausible distractor among the options. Infrared and radio waves occupy the low-frequency end of the spectrum and are orders of magnitude lower in frequency compared with X-rays. Higher frequency also means higher photon energy (E = hf), which explains why X-rays are more penetrating and ionising than UV, infrared or radio waves.

subject: Physics
question_text: When a red rose flower is observed in blue light, what colour does the observer see?
explanation: perceived colour depends on which wavelengths a surface reflects versus absorbs; pigments selectively reflect certain colours and absorb the rest. A red rose looks red under white light because its pigment reflects red wavelengths while absorbing blue and green light. Under pure blue illumination there are no red wavelengths to reflect, so the red pigments absorb the blue and little or no light is returned to the eye, causing the flower to appear black.\n\nHence 'Black' is correct; 'Red' cannot be seen because red perception requires red wavelengths in the incident light. 'Magenta' would require reflection of both red and blue, and 'Yellow' requires reflection of red and green — neither condition holds for a typical red pigment under only blue light. Only special cases (e.g., fluorescence that converts blue to red, or additional ambient white light) would change this result; under ideal blue-only illumination the flower appears black.

subject: Physics
question_text: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is 20μF in air and 60μF with dielectric. What is the dielectric constant?
explanation: the dielectric constant K is the ratio of the capacitance with a dielectric to the capacitance in air (or vacuum), K = C/C0. Here C0 = 20 μF (in air) and C = 60 μF (with dielectric), so K = 60/20 = 3. The microfarad units cancel in the ratio, so K is a dimensionless number equal to 3.\n\nA dielectric increases capacitance by polarising and reducing the effective electric field between the plates, therefore the capacitance is multiplied by K. Options 2, 0.3 and 6 are inconsistent with the given values because they would require C to be 40 μF, 6 μF or 120 μF respectively, none of which matches the data. Using air as the reference is acceptable at senior‑secondary level because air's permittivity is effectively the same as vacuum for this calculation.

Energy used in 6 hours: E = 0.5 kW × 6 h = 3 kWh.\n\nCost at ₦4 per kWh: Cost = 3 kWh × ₦4/kWh = ₦12, so ₦12 is correct. Why other options are wrong: ₦24 would occur if you doubled the power (treating 500 W as 1 kW so E = 6 kWh), ₦16 fits a mistaken time or energy of 4 kWh, and ₦0.12 comes from a decimal-place or unit error (not converting W to kW correctly). question_text: The bond between silicon and germanium is:
explanation:
Covalent bonding: atoms share electrons to form directional bonds, commonly producing network solids in metalloids and nonmetals.
Silicon and germanium are both Group 14 elements with four valence electrons and similar electronegativities, so they attain stable octets by sharing electrons rather than by electron transfer.
In the solid state Si and Ge form diamond‑like tetrahedral lattices where each atom is covalently bonded to four neighbours, giving the characteristic semiconductor structure.
Hence the Si–Ge bond is covalent, making “Covalent” the correct option because the atoms share electrons in a network structure.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which material has an increase in resistance with temperature?
explanation:
The concept is the temperature coefficient of resistance: metals typically have a positive coefficient, so their resistance increases with temperature.
In metals heating raises lattice vibrations (phonons) which scatter conduction electrons, reducing their mean free path and increasing resistivity.
Electrolytes and water are ionic conductors whose resistance usually decreases with temperature because increased ionization and ionic mobility raise conductivity.
Exceptions occur only in special conditions (for example superconductivity at very low temperatures or material phase changes), but under ordinary laboratory and everyday temperatures metals show increasing resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: The electrical properties of germanium can be altered drastically by impurities. The process is:
explanation:
Doping is the deliberate introduction of controlled impurity atoms into intrinsic germanium to change its electrical conductivity.
Donor impurities such as phosphorus (five valence electrons) produce n-type germanium by supplying extra electrons, while acceptors like boron (three valence electrons) produce p-type material by creating holes.
These impurity atoms introduce energy levels near the conduction or valence band, greatly increasing the number of free charge carriers and thus the semiconductor's conductivity.
Saturation is unrelated to impurity control, and 'bonding' refers to chemical bonding in general, not the controlled addition of impurities that defines doping.

subject: Physics
question_text: In a hydraulic press, the pump piston exerts a pressure of 100Pa on the liquid. What force is exerted on the second piston of cross-sectional area 3m²?
explanation: Pascal's principle — pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid and to the walls of its container. Pressure P is defined as force per unit area, P = F/A, with the SI unit Pascal (1 Pa = 1 N·m⁻2). The pump piston produces 100 Pa throughout the liquid, so the second piston experiences the same pressure and the force on it is F = P × A.\n\nCompute: F = 100 N·m⁻2 × 3 m² = 300 N, therefore the correct choice is 300 N. Option '100' mistakes pressure for force (100 Pa ≠ 100 N); '200' or '150' would result from using areas of 2 m² or 1.5 m² respectively, so they do not match the given 3 m². Unit check: Pa×m² gives N, confirming the calculation's dimensional consistency and that 300 N is the correct force.

subject: Physics
question_text: Heat transfer by vibration of molecules of the medium is:
explanation:
Conduction is the transfer of heat through direct molecular collisions and vibrations in the medium, especially important in solids.
In conduction energy flows from hotter to colder regions as neighbouring molecules exchange kinetic energy and through lattice vibrations (phonons).
In metals conduction is greatly aided by mobile free electrons that transport thermal energy efficiently, and the rate is given by Fourier's law q = -kA dT/dx.
Diffusion refers to mass transport of particles down concentration gradients and is not the mechanism for vibration-driven heat transfer, making conduction the correct answer.

question_text: The characteristic of a vibration that determines its intensity is the:

Amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium; a larger amplitude means more mass moves further and the vibration carries more energy. Quantitatively, wave intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude (I ∝ A²), so small changes in amplitude produce larger changes in intensity.\n\nFrequency (option A) gives the number of oscillations per second and determines pitch, not the energy per cycle, so it does not set intensity. Overtone (option B) refers to harmonics that change timbre or spectral content, and wavelength (option C) is related to frequency and wave speed; neither directly determines intensity. Therefore Amplitude (option D) is correct because it directly controls the energy and hence the intensity of the vibration.

subject: Physics
question_text: The coefficient of friction between two perfectly smooth surfaces is:
explanation:
Coefficient of friction µ is defined as the ratio of the frictional force F to the normal reaction N, µ = F/N.
For perfectly smooth surfaces the frictional (tangential) force is zero because there are no surface asperities to produce resistance, so µ = 0/N = 0.
This idealisation means both static and kinetic friction vanish, so no tangential resisting force opposes impending or actual motion between the surfaces.
In practice all surfaces possess microscopic roughness so measured coefficients are small but nonzero, making µ = 0 a theoretical idealisation used to simplify problems.

subject: Physics
question_text: Total internal reflection will not occur when light travels from:
options_json: ["Water to air","Water into glass","Glass to air","Glass into water"]
explanation:
Total internal reflection (TIR) occurs when light travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer one and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle θc given by sinθc = n2/n1 (n1>n2).
For water → glass the light goes from a medium of lower refractive index (water, n≈1.33) into a higher one (glass, n≈1.50), so it is from rarer to denser and there is no critical angle for TIR.
Because n1<n2 for water→glass, no incident angle will produce total internal reflection, which is why this option is correct as the case where TIR will not occur.
Therefore Water into glass is the only listed path that cannot produce total internal reflection, distinguishing it from the other three options.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which of the following obeys Ohm's law?
explanation:
Ohm's law states that for an ohmic conductor the potential difference V across it is proportional to the current I (V = IR), so the resistance is constant for fixed conditions.
Metals obey Ohm's law because conduction by free electrons gives a linear V–I relationship and a nearly constant resistance provided the temperature and physical state are steady.
The qualification 'constant temperature' is important: a metal's resistivity changes with temperature, so heating the conductor can cause departures from ideal linearity.
Glass is an insulating material with negligible current until breakdown or leakage paths occur, and therefore does not show a simple linear V–I relation and is not ohmic.

subject: Physics
question_text: The particle nature of light is demonstrated by the:
explanation:
The photoelectric effect demonstrates that light consists of discrete quanta (photons) because electrons are emitted from a metal only when incident light quanta have sufficient energy to overcome the work function.
Einstein's E = hf explanation predicts a threshold frequency and shows the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons depends on light frequency, not intensity, which is a signature of particle-like energy transfer.
Raising light intensity increases the number of emitted electrons (more photons) but not their individual energies, a result incompatible with a purely classical wave energy interpretation.
Diffraction and interference are characteristic wave behaviors that oppose a purely particle picture, so diffraction is not evidence of the particle nature of light.

Distance is a scalar that measures total path length travelled and does not include direction, so it cannot serve where direction is required.

subject: Physics
question_text: The quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of a body by 1K is the body's:
explanation: Heat capacity — the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of the entire body by 1 K. Definition and formula: heat capacity C = Q/ΔT, with SI unit joule per kelvin (J K⁻¹). Heat capacity is an extensive property that depends on the mass and material of the body; for a homogeneous object C = m·c (mass times specific heat capacity).\n\nSpecific heat capacity is the intensive form (c = Q/(mΔT)), giving heat per unit mass per kelvin, so it is not the same as the body's total heat capacity. Internal energy is the total microscopic energy of a system and is not defined as the heat needed to raise temperature by 1 K, although temperature changes affect internal energy. Latent heat is the heat involved in a phase change at constant temperature, so it does not quantify heat required to change temperature by 1 K.

explanation:

question_text: Capillarity (capillary action) occurs because of
option_b: The interplay between adhesion (liquid to tube) and cohesion (liquid to liquid) forces
option_c: Atmospheric pressure pushing liquid up the tube
option_d: The weight of liquid in the tube ✓
options_json: ["Only cohesion between liquid molecules","The interplay between adhesion (liquid to tube) and cohesion (liquid to liquid) forces","Atmospheric pressure pushing liquid up the tube","The weight of liquid in the tube ✓"]
answer_text: The interplay between adhesion (liquid to tube) and cohesion (liquid to liquid) forces
explanation:
Capillarity is the spontaneous rise or fall of a liquid in a narrow tube caused by surface tension arising from molecular adhesion and cohesion.
The correct option is the interplay between adhesion (liquid-to-tube) and cohesion (liquid-to-liquid): when adhesion exceeds cohesion the liquid climbs the tube and forms a concave meniscus, and when cohesion exceeds adhesion the liquid is depressed with a convex meniscus.
For example, water wets glass (adhesion > cohesion) so it rises in a capillary, whereas mercury does not wet glass (cohesion > adhesion) so it is depressed.
The weight of the liquid opposes capillary rise; an equilibrium height is reached when the upward force from surface tension (due to adhesion/cohesion) balances the downward weight of the liquid column.

explanation:
